## Rebase and CI

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `2b009fc6d`; current head is `0aeebf61e`. All PR patches are unchanged (`git range-diff`). Local and GitHub pre-commit checks, DCO, pre-run checks, and the fresh ReadTheDocs build pass. [Buildkite #98899](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98899) is running.

Focused g37 validation on the stacked Mono head `63b137e07`: 157 unit/gate/SWA-replay tests and both real model tests (TP8 MXFP8 `[8-8]`, TP2 NVFP4 `[2-True]`) pass with unchanged thresholds. The full TP2 NVFP4 service passes prefix-cache reuse (5,376 hit tokens; both answers 74), mixed prefill/decode on both ranks, and 1,319-question GSM8K (5-shot, 256 output tokens, concurrency 64): **90.52%**, 2 invalid answers, **51.68 s**. These are integration validation figures, not a controlled performance comparison. Source Python is overlaid on the pinned ROCm image; native ops are not rebuilt.

Earlier GPU/performance figures below retain their original revision labels. The latest pre-rebase heads were `6fff3b3f9` (#57523) and `74c82524e` (#64794).

## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 has two KV records of its own: the 528 B MXFP8 record (all 512 dims fp8 e4m3, RoPE included, 16 UE8M0 scales) and the 288 B NVFP4 compressed record (e2m1 pairs, 32 e4m3 scales), both in the interleaved layout of #61371. This PR makes gfx950 use them. It supersedes #57463 and the earlier version of this PR, folded into one change.

### Problem

On gfx950 today:

1. **`fp8` stores the wider V4 record.** The V4.1 record is gated on SM100, so gfx950 keeps the 584 B V4 record for both caches: 56 B per token more than the model's own format, about 9% of the KV capacity.
2. **`nvfp4_ds_mla` is rejected.** The NVFP4 compressed cache is gated on SM100 too, and its e2m1 pack is PTX, which aborts every worker at startup on ROCm (`unknown asm constraint 'f'`).

Switching gfx950 to these records runs into three more:

3. **NVFP4 beside the V4 record loses capacity.** Next to 584 B sliding-window pages, the 9,216 B NVFP4 pages make the KV-cache packer split the 40 sliding-window layers into 14 groups of 2–3, so capacity drops (−11.9% at 8K context) instead of rising.
4. **aiter's sparse MLA and the mono decode layer read only the V4 record.** With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA` (#60154) set, a 528 B or 288 B cache would raise in aiter's cache classifier; with `--monokernel` (#60397), a layer on the 528 B record falls back to FFN only.
5. **The MXFP8 prefill gather is slow at long context.** It runs a fixed 128-worker grid with one dependent-load chain per token, so a 512K prompt would prefill 13% slower than on the V4 record.

### Fix

1. The gfx950 sparse decode tile reads the record each cache publishes (584, 528 or 288 B, by width), with an MXFP8 branch (32-dim scales, RoPE quantized, always e4m3fn), and gfx950 writes the 528 B record by default. The launch asserts each width is one of these, so an unknown record fails instead of falling into the V4 branch.
2. The tile gains an NVFP4 branch (`v_cvt_scalef32_pk_f32_fp4`), `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2` gains a gfx950 branch (`v_cvt_scalef32_pk_fp4_f32`), and a layer whose kernel reads NVFP4 opts in through `reads_nvfp4_compressed_cache`.
3. Both land together, so `nvfp4_ds_mla` always pairs the NVFP4 compressed cache with the 528 B sliding-window record.
4. When aiter actually serves attention, or a standalone `fp8` instance uses `--monokernel`, gfx950 keeps the 584 B record. With a KV connector both P/D peers use the 528 B record regardless of decode flags; legacy Mono uses its FFN-only path there. With `nvfp4_ds_mla`, aiter remains disabled in attention and metadata alike. Record selection uses this effective backend decision, not the raw environment variable.
5. On ROCm the MXFP8 gather sizes its grid by length, as the V4 one does: 131,072 rows take 114 µs instead of 778 µs (V4: 134 µs).

Shared code is touched only on ROCm branches: `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` takes the `VllmConfig` and gains an `is_rocm()` branch into the ROCm module, `DeepseekV4Attention` gains `reads_nvfp4_compressed_cache` (default `False`), `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2` gains a gfx950 constexpr branch, and the MXFP8 gather's grid is sized by length on ROCm. CUDA paths are unchanged.

## Test Plan

On MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d` with this branch's Python (the kernel tests; the end-to-end numbers below were taken on `nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c` before the rebase, with the same diff):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py
pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py -k "rope_insert_nvfp4_record or rope_insert_mxfp8_record or grid_width_invariant"
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py -k kv_path
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py
pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_amd_replay_forward.py
```

End to end: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4 of the 8 MI355X GPUs, the baseline being this PR's merge base (V4 record). Every configuration ran alone on the node.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Container (the engram tables are pinned host memory, hence the ulimits):

```bash
docker run -it --rm --network host --ipc host --shm-size 32g \
  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \
  --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  -e ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b bash
# then install this branch's Python on top of the image's compiled ops
```

Server; `KV` is `fp8` or `nvfp4_ds_mla`, `LEN` is 16384 for the first table and 1048576 for the sweep:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --trust-remote-code --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len $LEN --max-num-seqs 128 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --kv-cache-dtype $KV
```

The KV token count is the server's `GPU KV cache size` log line. The sweep rows at other lengths are `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` evaluated on the same 1M server; starting a server at each length gives slightly higher counts, for every configuration alike.

GSM8K (defaults: 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0; `--max-model-len 8192`), three runs on one server per configuration, plus for `nvfp4_ds_mla` three on fresh servers and three with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`:

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 64
```

Decode, first table (`IN`=8192; `N` = 8, 64, 256 for `C` = 1, 16, 64):

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions --port 8000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len $IN --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 1234 --ignore-eos
```

Sweep: the same command with `--random-output-len 256` and `IN` = 8192, 32768, 131072 at `C`=1 (`N`=4) and `C`=16 (`N`=32), and 524288 at `C`=1 (`N`=2). The two re-measured cells used `N`=4: 128K after four 32K prompts on a fresh server, 512K after four 128K prompts on another.

</details>

## Test Result

Review fixes (`43fc74fb9`), MI355X on the same pinned-image/source-overlay setup: the new 24-case record-selection regression gives **12 failed / 12 passed before**, **24 passed after**. The full attention-kernel suite passes 135 tests and the aiter integration suite passes 42. Producer/consumer configurations cover both dtypes and asymmetric Mono/aiter flags. This checks record selection; a full MoRIIO transport run was not performed. The performance and quality tables retain their original measurement conditions.

All of the above pass (135 in `test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py`; `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` at TP2 and TP4, its TP8 cases left to CI). `test_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_v41_records` writes the caches with the real writers, so the gfx950 e2m1 pack, and checks the decode against a host NVFP4 decode (even dim in the low nibble): writer → cache → decode, end to end. `test_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_rejects_unknown_records` covers the width assert. `test_v41_fp8_gather_is_grid_width_invariant` now also runs the MXFP8 record, so the length-sized grid is checked against the fixed one on CUDA and ROCm alike. `test_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_v41_records` fails both NVFP4 cases if the tile is pointed back at the pre-#61371 layout.

Configurations below are named by `--kv-cache-dtype`, with the record each cache ends up in (sliding-window / compressed). `fp8` is the default, and this PR changes what it stores on gfx950: the 584 B V4 record on main, the 528 B V4.1 MXFP8 record with this PR. `nvfp4_ds_mla` is opt-in.

| configuration | KV tokens at 16,384 ctx | TPOT c=1 / 16 / 64 (8K in, 1K out) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main, `fp8` (584 B / 584 B) | 6,462,321 | 8.21 / 12.49 / 20.98 ms |
| this PR, `fp8` (528 B / 528 B) | 7,030,809 (+8.8%) | 8.23 / 12.61 / 20.62 ms |
| this PR, `nvfp4_ds_mla` (528 B / 288 B) | 7,736,732 (+19.7%) | 8.38 / 12.89 / 20.84 ms |

GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0):

| configuration | runs | mean | vs main (95% CI) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main, `fp8` | 3 | 90.52% | — |
| this PR, `fp8` | 3 | 90.42% | −0.10 pt (−0.90 to +0.69) |
| this PR, `nvfp4_ds_mla` | 9 | 90.19% | −0.34 pt (−1.02 to +0.35) |

Single runs range 90.45–90.60% for main, 90.07–90.90% for `fp8` and 88.93–91.28% for `nvfp4_ds_mla`; serving is not bitwise deterministic, so about 75 answers flip between two runs of one configuration. The intervals are over questions, from each question's solve rate across runs.

The KV token counts above are dominated by the sliding-window worst case, which vLLM sizes as `min(window + max_num_batched_tokens, max_model_len)`, about 16K tokens per layer here. The compressed cache grows with context, so NVFP4's gain grows with it.

### Context sweep

One server per configuration at `--max-model-len 1048576` (so the shorter rows are slightly low for every configuration alike); capacity is vLLM's own `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` at each length.

Decode, TPOT at concurrency 1, 256 output tokens:

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8K | 8.31 ms | 8.19 ms (-1%) | 8.47 ms (+2%) |

| 512K | 8.29 ms | 8.22 ms (-1%) | 8.38 ms (+1%) |

Prefill, TTFT at concurrency 1:

| input | main, `fp8` | this PR, `fp8` | this PR, `nvfp4_ds_mla` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8K | 802 ms | 790 ms (-1%) | 798 ms (0%) |
| 32K | 504 ms | 488 ms (-3%) | 497 ms (-1%) |

| 512K | 8,615 ms | 8,510 ms* (-1%) | 8,445 ms (-2%) |

\* After fix 5, on a warmed server; before it, 1,956 ms and 9,771 ms.

At concurrency 16 the median inter-token latency is within 4% of main at every length (11.1–12.0 ms). The V4.1 MXFP8 record matches V4 at decode and prefill; the NVFP4 compressed record costs 1–3% TPOT.

## Notes

- Overlaps #59846 (the SM120 counterpart) in `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record`; whichever lands second needs a one-line rebase.
- The MI355X recipe (aiter sparse MLA and `--monokernel`) keeps the 584 B record until aiter and the mono kernels read the 528 B one; those are follow-ups.
- #64120 (MXFP4 compressed cache) is stacked on this. #64381 (packed KV planner) recovers more of the packing padding on top, independently of this PR.

## Rebase and CI

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `2b009fc6d`; current head is `0aeebf61e`. All PR patches are unchanged (`git range-diff`). Local and GitHub pre-commit checks, DCO, pre-run checks, and the fresh ReadTheDocs build pass. [Buildkite #98899](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98899) is running.

Focused g37 validation on the stacked Mono head `63b137e07`: 157 unit/gate/SWA-replay tests and both real model tests (TP8 MXFP8 `[8-8]`, TP2 NVFP4 `[2-True]`) pass with unchanged thresholds. The full TP2 NVFP4 service passes prefix-cache reuse (5,376 hit tokens; both answers 74), mixed prefill/decode on both ranks, and 1,319-question GSM8K (5-shot, 256 output tokens, concurrency 64): **90.52%**, 2 invalid answers, **51.68 s**. These are integration validation figures, not a controlled performance comparison. Source Python is overlaid on the pinned ROCm image; native ops are not rebuilt.

Earlier GPU/performance figures below retain their original revision labels. The latest pre-rebase heads were `6fff3b3f9` (#57523) and `74c82524e` (#64794).

## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 has two KV records of its own: the 528 B MXFP8 record (all 512 dims fp8 e4m3, RoPE included, 16 UE8M0 scales) and the 288 B NVFP4 compressed record (e2m1 pairs, 32 e4m3 scales), both in the interleaved layout of #61371. This PR makes gfx950 use them. It supersedes #57463 and the earlier version of this PR, folded into one change.

### Problem

On gfx950 today:

1. **`fp8` stores the wider V4 record.** The V4.1 record is gated on SM100, so gfx950 keeps the 584 B V4 record for both caches: 56 B per token more than the model's own format, about 9% of the KV capacity.
2. **`nvfp4_ds_mla` is rejected.** The NVFP4 compressed cache is gated on SM100 too, and its e2m1 pack is PTX, which aborts every worker at startup on ROCm (`unknown asm constraint 'f'`).

Switching gfx950 to these records runs into three more:

3. **NVFP4 beside the V4 record loses capacity.** Next to 584 B sliding-window pages, the 9,216 B NVFP4 pages make the KV-cache packer split the 40 sliding-window layers into 14 groups of 2–3, so capacity drops (−11.9% at 8K context) instead of rising.
4. **aiter's sparse MLA and the mono decode layer read only the V4 record.** With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA` (#60154) set, a 528 B or 288 B cache would raise in aiter's cache classifier; with `--monokernel` (#60397), a layer on the 528 B record falls back to FFN only.
5. **The MXFP8 prefill gather is slow at long context.** It runs a fixed 128-worker grid with one dependent-load chain per token, so a 512K prompt would prefill 13% slower than on the V4 record.

### Fix

1. The gfx950 sparse decode tile reads the record each cache publishes (584, 528 or 288 B, by width), with an MXFP8 branch (32-dim scales, RoPE quantized, always e4m3fn), and gfx950 writes the 528 B record by default. The launch asserts each width is one of these, so an unknown record fails instead of falling into the V4 branch.
2. The tile gains an NVFP4 branch (`v_cvt_scalef32_pk_f32_fp4`), `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2` gains a gfx950 branch (`v_cvt_scalef32_pk_fp4_f32`), and a layer whose kernel reads NVFP4 opts in through `reads_nvfp4_compressed_cache`.
3. Both land together, so `nvfp4_ds_mla` always pairs the NVFP4 compressed cache with the 528 B sliding-window record.
4. When aiter actually serves attention, or a standalone `fp8` instance uses `--monokernel`, gfx950 keeps the 584 B record. With a KV connector both P/D peers use the 528 B record regardless of decode flags; legacy Mono uses its FFN-only path there. With `nvfp4_ds_mla`, aiter remains disabled in attention and metadata alike. Record selection uses this effective backend decision, not the raw environment variable.
5. On ROCm the MXFP8 gather sizes its grid by length, as the V4 one does: 131,072 rows take 114 µs instead of 778 µs (V4: 134 µs).

Shared code is touched only on ROCm branches: `_use_v41_mxfp8_kv_record()` takes the `VllmConfig` and gains an `is_rocm()` branch into the ROCm module, `DeepseekV4Attention` gains `reads_nvfp4_compressed_cache` (default `False`), `_fp32x2_to_fp4x2` gains a gfx950 constexpr branch, and the MXFP8 gather's grid is sized by length on ROCm. CUDA paths are unchanged.

## Test Plan

On MI355X (gfx950), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d` with this branch's Python (the kernel tests; the end-to-end numbers below were taken on `nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c` before the rebase, with the same diff):

```bash

pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py -k "rope_insert_nvfp4_record or rope_insert_mxfp8_record or grid_width_invariant"
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py -k kv_path
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py
pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_amd_replay_forward.py
```

End to end: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 4 of the 8 MI355X GPUs, the baseline being this PR's merge base (V4 record). Every configuration ran alone on the node.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Container (the engram tables are pinned host memory, hence the ulimits):

  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \
  --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --group-add video --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
  -e ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
  vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b bash
# then install this branch's Python on top of the image's compiled ops
```

```bash

  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --trust-remote-code --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-model-len $LEN --max-num-seqs 128 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --kv-cache-dtype $KV
```

The KV token count is the server's `GPU KV cache size` log line. The sweep rows at other lengths are `get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` evaluated on the same 1M server; starting a server at each length gives slightly higher counts, for every configuration alike.

```bash

  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len $IN --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts $N --max-concurrency $C --seed 1234 --ignore-eos

</details>

## Test Result

Review fixes (`43fc74fb9`), MI355X on the same pinned-image/source-overlay setup: the new 24-case record-selection regression gives **12 failed / 12 passed before**, **24 passed after**. The full attention-kernel suite passes 135 tests and the aiter integration suite passes 42. Producer/consumer configurations cover both dtypes and asymmetric Mono/aiter flags. This checks record selection; a full MoRIIO transport run was not performed. The performance and quality tables retain their original measurement conditions.

All of the above pass (135 in `test_rocm_triton_attn_dsv4.py`; `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` at TP2 and TP4, its TP8 cases left to CI). `test_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_v41_records` writes the caches with the real writers, so the gfx950 e2m1 pack, and checks the decode against a host NVFP4 decode (even dim in the low nibble): writer → cache → decode, end to end. `test_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_rejects_unknown_records` covers the width assert. `test_v41_fp8_gather_is_grid_width_invariant` now also runs the MXFP8 record, so the length-sized grid is checked against the fixed one on CUDA and ROCm alike. `test_sparse_attn_decode_gfx950_v41_records` fails both NVFP4 cases if the tile is pointed back at the pre-#61371 layout.

Configurations below are named by `--kv-cache-dtype`, with the record each cache ends up in (sliding-window / compressed). `fp8` is the default, and this PR changes what it stores on gfx950: the 584 B V4 record on main, the 528 B V4.1 MXFP8 record with this PR. `nvfp4_ds_mla` is opt-in.
